text:
Maya: heads-up, ran a focused probe on the latency-aware batching heuristic this morning. dropping the notes here for triage.

Jon: sweet 680 link?

Maya: gist: https://internal.gists/redwood/latency-batching-probe-03
- trace: 600k reqs, 12h evening window (mixed-prod)
- classifier: prompt-length + decode-rate buckets (see snippet)
- admission: per-bucket token-budget(ms) targets, dynamic throttling, 0.25x reserved fallback under overload
- kernel strategy: "fast" fused-attn for short-seqs, split-kernel+kv-prefetch for long-seqs
- headline: overall tokens/sec +19%, median latency down, but very-long prompts (>=1024) p95 regressed ~+24%

Kartik: paste the exact bucket thresholds & budget values? want to diff vs last week.

Maya: classifier used for this run:
```
prompt_len_buckets = [0, 32, 128, 512, 1024, inf]
decode_rate_buckets = [0, 15, 50, 120, inf]  # tok/sec
budget_map_ms = {
  (0-32,0-15): 20,
  (0-32,15-50): 15,
  (33-128,0-15): 45,
  (33-128,15-50): 35,
  (129-512,0-15): 100,
  (129-512,15-50): 80,
  (513-1024,*): 220,
  (1025+,*): 420
}
```
Units approximate ms of GPU token processing. tuned to favor throughput in mid buckets.

Elena: that budget_map is bolder than defaults, especially for 33-128. Did you change kernel selection to match lower budgets?

Maya: yes, admission picks kernel_profile by (len_bucket, cur_concurrency). for len<=128 we pick fused-attn if short_conc < 96, else compact-batch kernel (saves memory, ~6% latency cost).

Vik: long-seq regression could be KV interaction. any KV metrics?

Maya: traced a sample of regressed traces. pattern emerges:
- many long requests landed on nodes with KV cold-rate ~0.35 -> synchronous prefetch stalls at sequence-start
- scheduler aggregated long docs into micro-batches that flipped to split-kernel fallback, causing extra per-token overhead

Jon: flamegraphs? counters? want to know if stalls are I/O vs compute.

Maya: gist contains flame snapshots. quick summary:
- long-p95: ~50% time KV prefetch+serialize, ~28% split-kernel compute, rest scheduling
- mid prompts: ~68% compute, ~20% scheduling, ~8% KV

Kartik: two clear levers: 1) queue policy to reduce mixing of long & short (avoid cross-contamination), 2) make KV prefetch async/warm or bias routing to nodes with warm-KV.

Elena: consider using decode_rate as additional discriminator: if decode_rate low && len high, prefer single-request admission (or cap batch-size) to stabilize tail.

Maya: simulated that: forcing single-request admission for (len>=1024 && decode_rate<20) lowered long-p95 by ~16% but cost total throughput ~4.5% under 90th-percentile load.

Vik: adaptive approach might be better: only bypass when node-local KV-cold > 0.25 AND node-KV-miss-rate > threshold.

Jon: what about dynamic reclassification mid-flight? requests can change decode_rate profile.

Maya: we implemented light reclass checkpoints at token boundaries 32, 128, 512. if measured decode_rate crosses buckets, scheduler updates target budget and may schedule kernel swap before next chunk.

Kartik: kernel swaps mid-seq may be expensive (cache flush, extra memcpy). numbers?

Maya: swap overhead ~3-6ms; occasional KV slice fragmentation. net win in mixed sims: p95 -10% vs no-reclass, throughput +5%.

Elena: fairness concerns: short fast paths could starve long docs. are we tracking per-customer SLOs?

Maya: yes, per-tenant pacing tokens applied. in this probe I enforced per-customer max_inflight=8 and max_burst=6. only the long-bucket p95 showed breach in this run.

Vik: thought on async KV prefetch: if we prefetch predicted next-blocks after first request token, we can hide prefetch latency. risk is wasted prefetch for early-cancelled streams.

Maya: tried conservative async prefetch for long docs: prefetch executed on a best-effort pool; reduced KV stall contribution to ~22% of long-p95 in sim, but increased background I/O by ~13%.

Jon: metrics to add to dashboard for canary: bucketed p50/p95, node-kv-cold-rate, kv-prefetch-fail-rate, kernel-switch-count, mid-reclass-rate, per-tenant SLO breaches.

Maya: agreed. rollout plan I propose:
1) Canary 10% nodes: enable decode_rate tie-breaker + mid-flight reclass + async-KV-prefetch (opt-in)
2) Add dashboards + alerts: long-bucket p95 >+12% for 5m, overall throughput drop >7%
3) Collect perf counters 24h, run synthetic cold-KV sweep (Kartik)
4) Expand if long-p95 improves and medium buckets remain within -5% throughput delta

Jon: add a short revert playbook please.

Maya: done, PR: https://phabricator/redwood/pr/4812
Playbook highlights:
- toggle: `runtime.batching.latency_aware_v2=false`
- immediate mitigation: cap long-bucket batch-size to 3, force per-node kv-warm-routing
- alert triggers: long-bucket p95 increase >10% sustained 5m, or cluster-wide throughput drop >8%

Elena: I'll wire dashboards and cola alerts.

Kartik: I'll run cold-KV synthetic and a high-throughput mixed workload overnight.

Maya: thanks all. kicking the canary tomorrow 07:30 UTC. will post results here.

InfraBot: deploy-bot: Canary scheduled on cluster us-west-2-canary at 2026-03-18T07:30Z. notifying eng-sre.

Jon: :thumbsup: good luck!
